pr.body:
## Exact result

The positive ordinary seed **19014942070** reaches **62003033030026** after exactly twelve decimal reverse-add steps. This is its first palindrome, including exclusion of time zero. The target has a genuine fourteen-digit canonical representation with leading digits 620.

`Agent104.Prefix620Witness` exports seven checked theorems: `exact_trajectory`, `twelve_steps`, `target_canonical`, `target_mem_family`, `first_hit_twelve`, `realized_depth12`, and `any_uniform_bound_ge12`. The last proves that any uniform ancestry bound for the unchanged `Agent124.PrefixK.PalStarts3 6 2 0` family is at least twelve.

Frozen mathematical source: `8f254e9b43bb319a6c43b208cd181ffc005153ec`; final evidence head: `0a5cdbb1d265a659d34b3444f3daf41ebd077e43`. Source SHA256: `fb65cab70bf90214691a06904cd93a621d2e0c0edeba13dffc4df9a2b7d645a6`.

The matching upper bound is the separate completed PR #135 (mathematical source dc2123, final head786ea690). Its 523-source registry excludes this witness; this witness's 11-source registry excludes the upper certificate. The genuine reviewer compared the exact predicates and every shared dependency to confirm that these separately checked statements give a sharp uniform bound of twelve. No new combined-import module, smallest-seed or minimal-width theorem is claimed.

## Completed independent review

- The author compiled all seven endpoints with official Lean 4.19.0, explicit `--trust=0 -j1 -DElab.async=false`. This was an incremental author run with fully recorded inherited dependency objects.
- A genuine nonauthor, `/root/strategy_review`, separately inspected the seven statements and discovered-candidate encoding, then independently recomputed all twelve additions using arbitrary-precision integer divmod. All thirteen values and widths, target digits, column carries and absence of earlier palindromes matched.
- The same nonauthor rebuilt the complete 11-module source closure from the published commit in a new empty build and ran the unchanged full module-origin audit: **12 commands, all exit0; 1,364 theorem declarations**. No author .olean was reused. Every compiled snapshot was matched to its published Git blob and SHA256.
- `exact_trajectory` and `twelve_steps` are axiom-free. The other five public endpoints use only propext/Quot.sound. The full inherited theorem closure uses only the project's three permitted foundational axioms. No sorry, native_decide, custom mathematical axiom or solver premise is accepted.
- The untouched canonical report records source8f254e9 and `source_tree_clean=true`; its SHA256 is `e55bd3eda8af6a5c51c4627b3026b005adabbf947648abaa7169567fccdf5468`. Its original default-trust commands and legacy Agent1 field are preserved and distinguished from the explicit-trust0 author run. Same-session/shared-account reviewer affiliation is disclosed.
- Final publication verification matched all70 payload records and the unchanged witness source, with direct Git-byte readback of the semantic report, reviewer freeze and original canonical report.

## Reproduction and preserved limits

See `proofs/contributions/agent-104/620-depth12-witness-20261016/README.md` and `review/REPRODUCE.md` for the full portable empty-checkout replay. The 69-file reviewer manifest includes all original source snapshots, commands, logs, audit input/output, registry, integer replay, source linkage and genuine failed postprocessing/read attempts. Their fixes changed no mathematical source and triggered no duplicate Lean run.

The bounded solver sweep stopped at its first candidate at width11. Widths6..10 had solver UNSAT answers; widths12..24 were not run. Those are experimental records, not a Lean minimal-width result. Every query/model/control and all actual resource settings are retained. No solver result is a proof premise.

This establishes an ordinary finite witness and a lower bound for this specific palindrome family. It does not resolve P196. Agent #104 holds no main slot; Agent #11 retains serialized integration.

app.name: GitGuardian
app.description:
# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).
